sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Menifee County
sections.html:
Three offices in Frenchburg share the work. The elected appraiser, called the PVA, values each house. The sheriff mails the bill and collects it. The clerk takes over whatever is still unpaid when April 15 closes. Matching your question to the right desk gets you a payoff figure or a corrected value sooner.

The PVA, clerk and county attorney all use 12 Main Street, while the sheriff keeps a post office box of its own.

Each office has its own mailing box, so check the address before anything goes in the mail. Call ahead for office hours before you drive in.

Menifee County tax offices

The sheriff follows the statewide calendar in KRS 134.015. Bills arrive in the fall and go to whoever held title on January 1.

  • Through November 1: pay 2 percent less.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the bill as printed.
  • During January: 5 percent extra.
  • February 1 to April 15: a 21 percent combined penalty applies.
  • After April 15: the clerk holds the bill.

A house sold partway through the year still carries the earlier owner's name on that year's bill. Settle the split in the sales contract and ask the sheriff for the balance.

sections.h2: Menifee County housing and the market
sections.html:
Menifee is mountain country with about 204 square miles of land. Frenchburg is both the seat and the only city. Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge flank the county, and Lexington is under 70 miles away by the Mountain Parkway. National forest covers much of Menifee and farms cover about a tenth, so sellers mostly offer hillside lots, small tracts and cabins.

The county counted 6,113 residents in 2020, down from 6,306 ten years earlier, and a mid-2025 estimate of 6,430 would be a 5.2 percent rise. The 2020 count showed 3,277 housing units, 24.3 percent of them empty. Owners live in 75.5 percent of homes. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $125,800 and typical rent is $675. Monthly owner costs run $996 with a mortgage and $299 without one. If a remote address is for sale, ask what internet service it can get.

sections.h2: How to contest a Menifee County value
sections.html:
Sit down with the PVA first, and go to the clerk only if the two of you can't agree. Inspection starts on the first Monday in May and lasts two weeks, and filing closes one workday later.

A local board then hears the case within 25 to 35 days and gets five sitting days without state permission. A claim with no evidence must be denied, so bring paper:

  • Photos and contractor quotes for a worn roof or a shifting foundation on a slope.
  • Prices that comparable houses nearby fetched this past year.
  • Insurance policies or construction costs.

Audio recording of the hearing is allowed. A paid representative must belong to a group listed in KRS 133.120 and carry your signed authorization.

Owners aged 65 or older, and those classified as totally disabled, can claim it. File at the Menifee County PVA for the house you occupy. Each residential unit gets just one exemption under KRS 132.810, and manufactured homes count as units.

The exempt amount tracks a federal price index, so ask the PVA for the current figure. An approval granted after you paid brings a refund on the exempt slice. Report a sale or a death to the PVA, and whoever takes the house files anew.

On April 15 the sheriff passes the bill to the clerk and a lien goes on record. Interest starts at 1 percent each month, with a 10 percent clerk charge and a 20 percent county attorney charge on top. The clerk may sell the certificate to an outside investor from mid-July onward.

The county attorney can set up installments before a sale. After a sale you answer to the investor, who may add large fees. The January 1 owner owes the tax personally, and the lien can ride with the parcel for 11 years.

A 4 percent transient tax applies to short-term rentals, and the county's Departments page links the registration form and the monthly return. With Cave Run Lake and the Red River Gorge nearby, plenty of cabins fit that description.

A buyer who plans to rent will want those filings in order. If you hosted guests, gather your returns and tell the buyer what you filed. The county tourism office can explain how a new owner registers.

sections.h2: Selling a Menifee County house with tax owing
sections.html:
It can be done. An open bill, or one already at the clerk, becomes a payoff number that the sheriff or clerk will quote. Once the bill is at the clerk the number climbs monthly, so ask for a fresh quote close to closing.

Homes here are often inherited, remote or in need of work. To compare a listing with a cash offer, subtract repairs, carrying costs and back tax from each. Get the payoff in writing before you accept anything. Lenders may ask about storm repairs on an older house, so keep permits and receipts together. Household income in the county is $45,096 at the middle, which affects what local buyers can pay, so price with that in mind.

sections.h2: What to bring and who to ask
sections.html:
For a sale, collect your deed, the latest bill and any exemption approval. Ask the PVA to confirm the parcel details, the sheriff for the current balance, and the clerk whether any lien is recorded. If the house passed to you by inheritance, have the papers that show who may sign. Once the sale closes, tell the PVA about the change in ownership so the exemption is removed from the old owner and the new bill goes out correctly.

Expect hillside parcels and small tracts to raise questions about boundaries and access. A recent survey, or at least a clear description in the deed, helps a buyer and a title company agree on what is being sold. Cabins near the lake or the gorge may also draw buyers who want rental income, so have your transient tax filings ready if the house was ever rented to guests. Cash buyers can often close without repairs, which helps when a roof or foundation would otherwise hold up a lender-financed sale.

faqs.q: Who do I pay for Menifee County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay the Menifee County Sheriff at P.O. Box 142, Frenchburg, KY 40322, phone (606) 768-3875. Write the bill number on a mailed payment.

faqs.q: Which date ends the penalty-free window in Menifee County?
faqs.a: December 31. A bill paid by then costs its printed amount, and January adds 5 percent.

faqs.q: Where is an assessment appeal filed in Menifee County?
faqs.a: At the county clerk's office, after a conference with the PVA. The filing is due one workday after the May inspection period ends.

faqs.q: Does Menifee County give older owners a tax break?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Kentucky homestead exemption for owners 65 or older who live in the house. Apply at the PVA, 12 Main Street in Frenchburg.

faqs.q: Can the county take a house over a small unpaid bill?
faqs.a: After April 15 a lien is recorded, and collection may include selling the certificate to a private buyer. Speak with the county attorney early about installments.
